sections.h2: Visiting the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Find the office inside the courthouse in Manitowoc: 1010 S 8th Street, 1st Floor, Room 107, Manitowoc, WI 54220. Any deed, mortgage or mortgage satisfaction on a property in the county ends up here, and staff maintain the lasting index of what was filed.

The counter opens Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30. Recording itself happens daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, so don't show up at the last minute. Call 920-683-4660 with questions.

Employees won't write a deed for you or offer legal opinions. For an inherited home, a land contract or a cloudy title, ask a Wisconsin attorney or your closing title company to prepare the papers first.

Manitowoc County counted 81,359 residents in 2020, with an estimate of 81,710 for July 2025. Roughly 24.8 percent are 65 or older, so a good share of listings come from families dealing with a parent's house. There are 38,298 housing units and 77.1 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $186,900, and typical gross rent runs $797 a month.

With values in that range, a $30 recording charge and the state transfer fee barely register next to repairs and holding costs. The filing steps don't change whether the house is worth $90,000 or $400,000.

Each deed you record costs $30, paid up front. A copy of a recorded document runs $2 for page one and $1 for every page beyond it, and certifying a copy adds $1. State law fixes these base charges for all Wisconsin counties.

ChargeAmount
Deed or mortgage recording$30 per document
Copy of a filed document$2 first page, $1 per added page
Certification of a copy$1 extra
Subdivision or condominium plat$50
State transfer fee on a sale30 cents per $100 of value

Search or special handling charges beyond these are set by the office, so ask the Register of Deeds for its current schedule.

sections.h2: How the state transfer fee works
sections.html:
On most sales the seller, called the grantor, pays the state transfer fee: 30 cents per $100 of value, rounded up for any partial $100 (Wis. Stat. 77.22). The register takes payment when you hand in the deed and notes the amount on the deed itself. The county keeps twenty percent and sends the remainder to the state.

Nobody at the counter audits your sale price. The statute says the register has no duty to work out the real value or to test whether an exemption applies, which puts the responsibility on whoever signs the return.

Certain transfers owe nothing. Section 77.25 exempts, among others:

  • Property passing through a will, descent or survivorship.
  • Family transfers for little or no payment, such as parent to child or grandparent to grandchild.
  • Real estate valued at $1,000 or less.
  • Foreclosure deeds, and deeds in lieu of foreclosure, going to a mortgage holder or land contract seller.
  • A transfer resulting from a sale for unpaid taxes or assessments.

An exempt deed must carry the matching subsection of 77.25 on its face.

Under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m), the office can turn away a document that strays from the standard layout. Before you submit, go through these points:

  • Title the document clearly, positioned 0.5 inch to 6 inches below the top edge of page one.
  • Leave a 3 inch by 3 inch empty box at the top right of page one for the recording stamp.
  • Put return information on page one, except when recording electronically.
  • Use white paper, 20 pound or heavier, 8.5 inches wide, cut to 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Print in black, blue or red ink, with no pages hinged or joined at the top or sides.
  • List who drafted the instrument.
  • Type or write the grantor, grantee and notary names legibly.

Remove any Social Security number before filing, since subsection (1m) bars recording a document that shows one. When a bundle of papers is submitted as one transaction and a single page fails these rules, the whole bundle may come back unrecorded.

sections.h2: Can a deed be e-recorded here?
sections.html:
It can. The county names four approved vendors, and each runs its own enrollment: Simplifile (713-210-4323), Hopdox (385-501-5103), Indecomm (651-765-6400) and EPN (888-325-3365). When a title company or closing attorney manages your sale, they'll likely send the deed through one of those.

A Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return (ERETR) is required for every deed too. Save it before you press submit, then print the receipt. That receipt has to accompany the original deed at the counter, and closing the page without printing means starting the return over.

Ask the office for its free alert service. You get notice whenever a paper is recorded under your name or against your property, which lets you check that it's real. The county calls real estate fraud uncommon in Wisconsin, and enrollment is a single call to 920-683-4660.

Alerts earn their keep for absentee owners, for empty inherited houses, and for anyone mid-sale. After your own deed is filed, the alert keeps watch for later filings.

sections.h2: Order of steps on a sale
sections.html: A typical Manitowoc County closing runs in a fixed order. The seller signs a deed that meets the layout rules. Someone files the electronic transfer return, usually the closing agent, and prints the receipt. The deed and receipt then go to the counter or through an e-recording vendor, with the $30 fee and any transfer fee paid. Last, the register stamps the document and adds it to the permanent index. A buyer paying cash skips the lender's mortgage, so there is one less document to record, but the deed and return are still needed. Ask for a copy of the filed deed afterward, since certified copies cost only $1 extra.

Run through a few things so you only make one trip. Compare the deed with the layout points above and confirm no Social Security number appears. Complete the electronic transfer return and print its receipt. Pack the $30 recording fee along with the transfer fee, unless the deed cites a 77.25 exemption. A title company closing your sale normally takes care of this; so does the closing agent for a cash buyer. If a detail on your document puzzles you, phone 920-683-4660 first.

faqs.q: Where is the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in the courthouse at 1010 S 8th Street, 1st Floor, Room 107, Manitowoc, WI 54220. The phone is 920-683-4660. Recording runs daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost here?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per document, paid in advance. A non-exempt sale also owes the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value. Copies are $2 for page one and $1 for each added page, plus $1 to certify.

faqs.q: Is anything filed with the state before recording?
faqs.a: Yes. File the Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return and print the receipt, which goes with the original deed. Only conveyances exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(1) or (10m) skip it.

faqs.q: Does passing down an inherited house owe the transfer fee?
faqs.a: Typically no. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11). If the heir then sells to a buyer, that second conveyance carries the fee based on the price.

faqs.q: Can I use e-recording in Manitowoc County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile, Hopdox, Indecomm or EPN, each of which has its own sign-up number. Your title company or closing attorney can tell you whether they'll file the deed that way.
